process_area.title: Responsible AI — Fairness, Explainability, Privacy & Safety

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Data Science (links to VS-30.2), Model Risk (links to VS-21), Legal (links to VS-100), Privacy (links to VS-91), business AI owners (fraud VS-125, credit/financing VS-38, HR-adjacent VS-23/VS-19)
fields.Trigger: Model build/validation (links to W3932); protected-class exposure
fields.Volume: Fairness testing of all rights/customer-affecting models

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "AI Governance/Data-Science define fairness metrics and protected attributes/proxies relevant" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document disparities, and require mitigation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "AI Governance/Legal document fairness outcomes for RA 10173/non-discrimination defense" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-615 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible AI — Fairness, Explainability, Privacy & Safety (PA-128.2).)
- operational: bias testing and mitigation; operational: proxy analysis
Pain Points / Risks: - **Disparate-impact risk**: Model declines/charges customers disparately by protected group (links to VS-91/VS-85); mitigated by bias testing and mitigation
- **Proxy-discrimination risk**: Non-protected features act as proxies; mitigated by proxy analysis
System Touchpoints: - ML platform (links to VS-30.2); model registry (links to W3931); fraud (links to VS-125); credit (links to VS-38); LP/HR (links to VS-23/VS-19); privacy (links to VS-91); mandatory discount (links to VS-85)
Time Estimate: - ~3–10 days per model fairness cycle + periodic retest

steps.activity: AI Governance/Data-Science define fairness metrics and protected attributes/proxies relevant to BuildRight (gender, age, region/income-proxy, mandatory-discount populations links to VS-85) per use-case: fraud-decline parity (links to VS-125), credit decision fairness (links to VS-38), pricing/promo fairness, LP/HR-adjacent model fairness (links to VS-23/VS-19)

AI Governance/Data-Science run bias testing pre-deployment and in production (links to W3947), document disparities, and require mitigation (reweighting, threshold adjustment, feature removal) before approval
steps.r: AI Governance / Data Science / Model Risk

steps.activity: AI Governance/Legal document fairness outcomes for RA 10173/non-discrimination defense (links to VS-91/VS-22) and report fairness pass-rates to the AI steering and AI ethics review board (links to W3952)

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Data Science (links to VS-30.2), Legal (links to VS-100), Privacy (links to VS-91), CX (links to VS-13), business AI owners (fraud VS-125, credit VS-38)
fields.Trigger: Adverse-decision model (links to W3931); transparency need

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "AI Governance/Data-Science provide model explainability appropriate to impact" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "AI Governance/Legal/CX provide customer-facing transparency and reason-codes for adverse" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "AI Governance maintain model cards / documentation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-615 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible AI — Fairness, Explainability, Privacy & Safety (PA-128.2).)
- operational: explainability requirements; operational: accuracy control
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unexplainable-decision risk**: Adverse decision cannot be explained (RA 10173/Consumer Act exposure — links to VS-91/VS-22); mitigated by explainability requirements
- **Misleading-disclosure risk**: Model card overstates capability; mitigated by accuracy control
System Touchpoints: - ML/explainability tools (links to VS-30.2); model registry/cards (links to W3931); fraud (links to VS-125); credit (links to VS-38); CX (links to VS-13); privacy (links to VS-91); legal (links to VS-100)
Time Estimate: - ~2–5 days per model + per-decision-type reason-code setup

steps.activity: AI Governance/Data-Science provide model explainability appropriate to impact: global (feature importance) and local (per-decision reasons) for adverse decisions — fraud decline (links to VS-125), credit decline (links to VS-38), pricing, and LP flags (links to VS-23)

AI Governance/Legal/CX provide customer-facing transparency and reason-codes for adverse automated decisions (RA 10173 automated-decision rights — links to VS-91), and a human-review channel (links to W3941)
AI Governance maintain model cards / documentation (purpose, data, performance, limitations, intended use) per model (links to W3931), and ensure disclosure is accurate and not misleading

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Privacy/DPO (links to VS-91), Data Governance (links to VS-29/VS-28.2), Legal (links to VS-100), Security (links to VS-27.3), business AI owners (CDP VS-126, fraud VS-125, personalization VS-126/W3892)
fields.Trigger: AI use of personal data; profiling/automated decision
fields.Volume: AI data-use governance across all PII-touching models

workflows.name: AI Data Governance, Privacy (RA 10173) & Consent for Profiling

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-register of "register high-risk processing with NPC where required" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "AI Governance/Privacy ensure AI profiling/automated decisions have valid consent" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document data provenance per model" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-147 (ensure AI model risk & human-oversight control.)
- operational: DPIA and consent; operational: minimization and testing
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unlawful-profiling risk**: AI profiles customers without consent/lawful basis (RA 10173 exposure — links to VS-91); mitigated by DPIA and consent
- **Training-data-leakage risk**: Customer PII leaks via model outputs/memorization; mitigated by minimization and testing
System Touchpoints: - Privacy/DPIA (links to VS-91/W389); data governance (links to VS-29/VS-28.2); CDP consent (links to VS-126/W3885); DSAR (links to VS-126/W3900); legal (links to VS-100); security (links to VS-27.3)

steps.activity: AI Governance/Privacy run a DPIA for AI/ML processing personal data (profiling, personalization, fraud scoring, CV/face — links to VS-91/W389), establish lawful basis and purpose-limitation, and register high-risk processing with NPC where required

AI Governance/Privacy ensure AI profiling/automated decisions have valid consent or lawful basis under RA 10173 (links to VS-91/W3885 CDP consent center), honor objection/DSAR rights (links to VS-126/W3900), and minimize/pseudonymize PII in training/inference

AI Governance/Data-Governance govern AI training data quality/lineage (links to VS-28.2/VS-29), prevent unlawful re-use (e.g., scraping customers' data into models), and document data provenance per model
steps.r: AI Governance / Data Governance / Data Science

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Data Science (links to VS-30.2), Model Risk (links to VS-21), Security (links to VS-27.3), business AI owners, IT (links to VS-27)
fields.Trigger: Model deployment (links to W3932); failure/adversarial event

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-test of "test model robustness" for safety/revenue-critical models (forecast VS-127, fraud VS-125, pricing) (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-extract of "model theft/extraction, and membership inference" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "define and test failover/fallback" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-615 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible AI — Fairness, Explainability, Privacy & Safety (PA-128.2).)
- operational: adversarial testing and security controls; operational: drift monitoring (links to W3947) and fail-safe
Pain Points / Risks: - **Adversarial-attack risk**: Bad actors evade fraud models or jailbreak GenAI (links to VS-125); mitigated by adversarial testing and security controls
- **Silent-failure risk**: Model degrades without detection, causing wrong decisions; mitigated by drift monitoring (links to W3947) and fail-safe
System Touchpoints: - ML platform (links to VS-30.2); security (links to VS-27.3); data quality (links to VS-28.2); fraud (links to VS-125); forecast (links to VS-127); incident mgmt (links to W3943); monitoring (links to W3947)
Time Estimate: - ~3–7 days per model robustness cycle + continuous

steps.activity: AI Governance/Data-Science test model robustness: edge cases, distribution shift, data quality degradation (links to VS-28.2), failure modes, and define fail-safe behavior (fallback to rules/human — links to W3941) for safety/revenue-critical models (forecast VS-127, fraud VS-125, pricing)
steps.r: AI Governance / Data Science / Model Risk

steps.activity: AI Governance/Security govern adversarial-AI threats: prompt injection/jailbreak (GenAI), data poisoning (training), model evasion (fraud links to VS-125), model theft/extraction, and membership inference (privacy links to VS-91)
AI Governance define and test failover/fallback (model down → revert to deterministic rules/human), and integrate with incident management (links to W3943) and monitoring (links to W3947)

fields.Participants: AI Governance, business AI owners (fraud VS-125, credit VS-38, LP VS-23, CX VS-13), Data Science (links to VS-30.2), Legal (links to VS-100), HR (links to VS-19)
fields.Trigger: High-impact/risk-tier model (links to W3931); adverse decision

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "AI Governance/business-owners define the human-oversight level per model/risk-tier" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review channels for adverse automated decisions" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalate high override rates to model owners for recalibration" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-615 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible AI — Fairness, Explainability, Privacy & Safety (PA-128.2).)
- operational: mandatory human-review for tier-1; operational: human-review for tier-1; operational: override-rate tracking and SLA
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-automation risk**: High-impact decisions fully automated without human review (RA 10173/Consumer Act — links to VS-91/VS-22); mitigated by mandatory human-review for tier-1
- **Rubber-stamp risk**: Human review is nominal; mitigated by override-rate tracking and SLA
System Touchpoints: - Model registry/tier (links to W3931); fraud case (links to VS-125/W3860); credit (links to VS-38); LP (links to VS-23); CX (links to VS-13); privacy/human-review (links to VS-91); monitoring (links to W3947)

steps.activity: AI Governance/business-owners define the human-oversight level per model/risk-tier: human-in-the-loop (approve), human-on-the-loop (monitor/override), human-out-of-the-loop (automated w/ audit), based on impact and reversibility

AI Governance/business-owners operate human-review channels for adverse automated decisions (fraud block review links to VS-125/W3860, credit decline review links to VS-38, LP flag review links to VS-23), ensuring timeliness and the customer's right to human review (links to W3938/VS-91)
AI Governance track override rates and human-review outcomes as a model-health and oversight-effectiveness signal (links to W3947), and escalate high override rates to model owners for recalibration

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Data Science (links to VS-30.2), Legal/IP (links to VS-100), Security (links to VS-27.3), Privacy (links to VS-91), Marketing (links to VS-14), CX (links to VS-13), HR (links to VS-19)

workflows.name: Generative AI & Content Governance (IP, Hallucination, Misuse)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "review, and disclaimers" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-generate of "AI Governance/HR/Security govern GenAI acceptable use by employees" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-615 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible AI — Fairness, Explainability, Privacy & Safety (PA-128.2).)
- operational: grounding and review; operational: IP governance and vendor terms
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hallucination-harm risk**: GenAI gives wrong product/price/safety info to customers (links to VS-22 Consumer Act); mitigated by grounding and review
- **IP-infringement risk**: GenAI outputs infringe third-party IP; mitigated by IP governance and vendor terms
System Touchpoints: - GenAI platform (links to VS-30.2); vendor AI (links to W3934); CX chatbot (links to VS-13); product content (links to VS-01.3); how-to (links to VS-09.1); security (links to VS-27.3); fraud/deepfake (links to VS-125); L&D (links to VS-19.4)

steps.activity: AI Governance/Legal govern GenAI output IP and liability: ownership of outputs, IP-infringement risk (third-party content), confidentiality of inputs (no trade secrets/PII into vendor models — links to VS-91/W3934), and contractual allocation with vendors

AI Governance/Data-Science manage hallucination/accuracy risk for GenAI use-cases (customer-service chatbot links to VS-13, product-info/description links to VS-01.3, how-to content links to VS-09.1): grounding/RAG, source-citation, accuracy review, and disclaimers
steps.r: AI Governance / Data Science / Business Owners

steps.activity: AI Governance/HR/Security govern GenAI acceptable use by employees (tool access, data-input rules, disclosure of AI-generated content — links to VS-19.4/W3930), and monitor for misuse (e.g., AI-generated phishing/deepfake against BuildRight — links to VS-27.3/VS-125)

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Security (links to VS-27.3), Privacy/DPO (links to VS-91), Legal (links to VS-100), business AI owners, Data Science (links to VS-30.2), CX (links to VS-13), Internal Audit (links to VS-21), Corporate Affairs (links to VS-14.3)
fields.Volume: ~dozens of AI incidents/yr (model failure, bias finding, hallucination harm)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-classify of "classify AI incidents" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-notify of "notify affected customers/regulators within timelines" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "AI Governance run post-incident review" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-615 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible AI — Fairness, Explainability, Privacy & Safety (PA-128.2).)
- operational: monitoring (links to W3947) and incident reporting; operational: triage protocol
Pain Points / Risks: - **Late-detection risk**: AI harm goes undetected; mitigated by monitoring (links to W3947) and incident reporting
- **Notifiable-breach-miss risk**: Model-related PII breach not reported to NPC (links to VS-91); mitigated by triage protocol
System Touchpoints: - Incident mgmt/security (links to VS-27.3); privacy/breach (links to VS-91/W53); legal (links to VS-100); CX (links to VS-13); audit (links to VS-21); corp affairs (links to VS-14.3); monitoring (links to W3947)

steps.activity: AI Governance/Security triage and classify AI incidents (model failure, drift breach, bias/disparate impact, hallucination harm, adversarial attack, privacy breach via model — links to VS-91/W53), and activate response (disable/revert/fallback — links to W3940)

AI Governance/Privacy/Legal assess reportability (RA 10173 data breach to NPC if model exposed PII — links to VS-91, consumer harm — links to VS-22) and notify affected customers/regulators within timelines
steps.r: AI Governance / Privacy / Legal / Corp Affairs

steps.activity: AI Governance run post-incident review (root cause links to W3947), remediate (model fix, control, policy), and capture learning to prevent recurrence, reporting material incidents to the Audit Committee (links to VS-21/VS-36)

fields.Participants: AI Governance, Compliance (links to VS-22), Legal (links to VS-100), Privacy (links to VS-91), Government Affairs (links to VS-104), Risk (links to VS-21), Data Science (links to VS-30.2)

workflows.name: AI Regulatory & Standards Monitoring (ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, future PH AI rules)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitor the AI regulatory and standards landscape" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-measure of "align the AI program to standards" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-generate of "prepare for future compliance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-615 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible AI — Fairness, Explainability, Privacy & Safety (PA-128.2).)
- operational: radar and readiness; operational: ISO 42001/NIST AI RMF alignment
Pain Points / Risks: - **Regulatory-surprise risk**: Future PH AI regulation catches BuildRight unprepared; mitigated by radar and readiness
- **Standards-lag risk**: Program not aligned to recognized standards; mitigated by ISO 42001/NIST AI RMF alignment
System Touchpoints: - Compliance (links to VS-22); privacy/NPC (links to VS-91); government affairs (links to VS-104); legal (links to VS-100); risk (links to VS-21); maturity (links to W3936)

steps.activity: AI Governance/Compliance/Gov-Affairs monitor the AI regulatory and standards landscape: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI Management System), NIST AI RMF, OECD AI Principles, and emerging PH/regional AI regulation (NPC guidance on automated decisions links to VS-91, potential PH AI act), and assess impact

AI Governance/Compliance align the AI program to standards (ISO 42001 certification readiness where valuable, NIST AI RMF functions: govern/map/measure/manage), and close gaps (links to W3936 maturity)

AI Governance/Legal/Gov-Affairs engage regulators/industry associations on AI policy (links to VS-104), and prepare for future compliance (registration, transparency obligations, fundamental-rights impact assessment)
